gnaw-swarm.name: Gnaw Swarm
gnaw-swarm.statLine: Swarmling · T1 · Mesoscopic cluster · MT 12 · MI 10 · soak 0 · BD 1 Lytic · pool 3d · PP 2 · Segments 6
gnaw-swarm.traits: Scent-Led (never Blind for more than one Cycle if it has smelled you) · Corrodes (any hit: target graft −1 soak until repaired)
special: Special — Swarm Over (2 PP): all live segments Strike one creature in Contact. Each Strike at −2 dice. Against a braced target this is a meat grinder; against a moving target it usually misses.
gnaw-swarm.weakness: area damage, Dry Zones, and any Thermal effect end Segments 1-for-1 with no Overflow needed.
gnaw-swarm.harvest: C3 / G1 · Codon 1.5 · BSP 1 (the C is worth 15 S; a Cohort that ignores these bodies is throwing money away)
gnaw-swarm.tactics: flows over everything, bites once per Cycle per two segments, and cannot be frightened.

detritus-feeder.name: Detritus Feeder
detritus-feeder.statLine: Swarmling · T1 (T2 in the Wastes) · MT 12 · MI 10 · soak 0 · BD 1 Lytic · pool 3d · PP 2 · Segments 6
detritus-feeder.traits: Acid-Immune (Lytic damage 0) · Harvest Instinct (it will spend its action on a corpse rather than on you — this is exploitable)
special: Special — Render (2 PP): on a corpse within Contact, it Harvests: the corpse's remaining Harvest value drops by one grade, and the Feeder grows: +2 Segments permanently.
detritus-feeder.weakness: if you deny it corpses (burn them, salt them, take them) it becomes a nuisance instead of a threat.
detritus-feeder.harvest: C3 / G1 · Codon 1.5 · BSP 1 (run it as Tier 2 in the Wastes and it yields C4 / G1, Codon 3.5 — which is why Reclaimer crews count the ground before they count the swarm)
detritus-feeder.tactics: ignores the fight, eats the battlefield. In a long fight, a Feeder becomes four Feeders.

protease-locusts.name: Protease Locusts
protease-locusts.statLine: Swarmling · T2 · MT 13 · MI 14 · soak 0 · BD 2 Lytic · pool 4d · PP 2 · Segments 8
protease-locusts.traits: Cloud Flight (Flow 5; ignores ground terrain) · Enzyme Rain (when a Strike hits, splashes 1 Lytic to everything in the band)
special: Special — Bloom Chorus (3 PP, once per Pulse War): all Locust swarms in the region (Director's count, usually 2–5 tokens) Strike the same target at once, adding +1 Overflow each.
protease-locusts.weakness: Turbid or Dry terrain grounds them; Hypertonic air costs them 1 PP per Cycle.
protease-locusts.tactics: arrives as a sound, strips a site's organic structure in four Cycles, and leaves before the Wardens do.

cytoplasmic-bleeder.name: Cytoplasmic Bleeder
cytoplasmic-bleeder.statLine: Standard · T1 · Microscopic-Mesoscopic · MT 13 · MI 22 · soak 1 · BD 2 Lytic · pool 4d · PP 3 · Flow 4
cytoplasmic-bleeder.traits: Attach (a hit gives it 1 Barb: it rides on the target, and while Barbed it Strikes for free at −1 die each Cycle, taking Reactive Osmosis damage from the host's own efforts)
special: Special — Tap (2 PP): drains 3 MI from the host and heals itself for that amount. Costs 1 ATP the first time (it has no ATP pool; track this as a 3-use limit per fight).
cytoplasmic-bleeder.weakness: Detach is one OSM contest (AT 14) or a Thermal/Lytic burn; Phagocyte Engulfment is fatal.
cytoplasmic-bleeder.harvest: C4 / G1 / P1 · Codon 3 · BSP 2 (its Greater Organ is the Tap Valve: Lytic family, +2 soak, and a Minor Cost of hunger)
cytoplasmic-bleeder.tactics: finds the slowest organism, attaches, and lets its allies do the killing.

enzymatic-horror.name: Enzymatic Horror
enzymatic-horror.statLine: Standard · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 Lytic · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 4
enzymatic-horror.traits: Acidic Surge (Core VII: once per Cycle, everything in Contact takes 5 Lytic) · Corrodes · Testate-Soft (Lytic weapons gain +2 against armour-wearers nearby)
special: Special — Dissolve Armour (3 PP): one target in Contact: its grafts lose 2 soak permanently (reparable by a Smith or a Nucleoid rite) and it gains Brittle.
enzymatic-horror.weakness: Mucoid-family grafts are immune to its Corrodes; Diver Gradient or a Desiccation zone halves its Surge.
enzymatic-horror.harvest: C5 / G2 / P1 · Codon 7 · BSP 2 (the Pristine Sequence is Acid Gland: the raw material of Acidic Corrosor kit)
enzymatic-horror.tactics: walks at the armour. It will pick the most armoured opponent, every time.

autolytic-hulk.name: Autolytic Hulk
autolytic-hulk.statLine: Standard · T3 · Macroscopic · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Lytic · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 3
autolytic-hulk.traits: Autophagic (when it takes 8+ damage, its next Strike gains +2 BD — it converts damage to appetite) · Segment Split (at 0 MI it does not die: it splits into 2 Swarmlings at full Segments, and the fight continues)
special: Special — Rupture Burst (4 PP, once): it detonates: `8 + Overflow` Lytic to everything in its band, then becomes a Swarmling with 6 Segments.
autolytic-hulk.weakness: killing it far from anyone; Desiccation (no fluid to rupture with); freezing.
autolytic-hulk.tactics: it wants to be hit while you are close. Deny it that and it is just slow.

swarm-of-nine-mouths.name: Swarm Of Nine Mouths
swarm-of-nine-mouths.statLine: Elite · T2 · Macroscopic colony · MT 15 · MI 60 · soak 4 · BD 4 Lytic · pool 6d · PP 4 · Flow 5 · Segments 12 (as a single organism)
swarm-of-nine-mouths.traits: Nine Digestions (each Cycle it chooses one damage type — Lytic, Thermal, Osmotic — and its attacks become that type; it reads what the Cohort is armoured against first) · Cannot be Flank-Breached
special: Special — Devour (5 PP, once per Pulse War): a Dormant or grappled creature is consumed: it goes to Total Lysis, and the Swarm gains +12 MI and one of the victim's Harvest traits for the rest of the fight.
swarm-of-nine-mouths.weakness: its Segment count is its action economy: area effects do not just damage it, they silence its specials.
swarm-of-nine-mouths.harvest: C8 / G3 / P2 / T1 · Codon 14 · BSP 4
swarm-of-nine-mouths.tactics: Cycle 1 reads your armour, Cycle 2 picks the type you cannot soak, Cycle 3 eats someone.

lysophage.name: Lysophage
lysophage.statLine: Elite · T3 · Macroscopic · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Lytic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 4
lysophage.traits: Enzyme Corridor (the fluid in a line 4 Drifts long becomes Acidic for its allies and costs the Cohort 3 Lytic/Cycle) · Graft-Eater (a hit removes 1 point of a target's graft soak permanently until repaired)
special: Special — Digest Apparatus (3 PP): one target's Apparatus in Contact is dissolved (durability roll 2d6, ≤7 destroys). It gains +1 BD for the rest of the fight.
lysophage.weakness: fight it without Apparatus (Lash-and-soak, Bursts, Desiccation); Smith Overcharge on its own dissolved gear.
lysophage.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4 (the Terminal Codon is why a Hegemony foundry will pay 600 S for this kill)
lysophage.tactics: disarms, then eats. A Lysophage fight that lasts six Cycles has left the Cohort unarmed.

recession-feeder.name: Recession Feeder
recession-feeder.statLine: Standard · T4 · Vast · MT 16 · MI 46 · soak 4 · BD 5 Lytic · pool 7d · PP 3 · Flow 3
recession-feeder.traits: Anti-Bloom (all regeneration, Segment regrowth, and healing within 6 Drifts of it stops) · Starving (it is always at 1 ATP; it will abandon any objective to eat)
special: Special — Draw In (4 PP): everything in a 5-Drift zone is pulled 1 band toward it and takes 6 Osmotic; it then heals 1 MI per creature affected.
recession-feeder.weakness: it is losing. A Cohort that feeds it (a corpse, a sacrificial animal, a colony's store) can lead a Recession Feeder somewhere useful.
recession-feeder.tactics: walks into a bloom and ends it, then turns on whoever is standing nearest.

bloom-matriarch.name: Bloom Matriarch
bloom-matriarch.statLine: Catastrophe · T2 · Vast · PHASE 1 MT 12 · MI 60 · soak 5 · BD 6 Lytic · pool 6d · PP 5 · Flow 2 (rooted)
bloom-matriarch.traits: Brood Sac (at the end of each Cycle, spawns 1 Swarmling T2 with half Segments; the sac must be cut — a Strike at AT 16, 20 S of acid, or a Breacher's charge to stop the spawning) · Rooted (it cannot be pushed; its Folds anchor it to the ground)
special: Special — Bloom Surge (5 PP, once per phase): all its Swarmlings act immediately, and the ground in a 6-Drift zone becomes a spore bed (4 Lytic/Cycle).
Special — Chemical Veil (3 PP): for 2 Cycles, Lytic damage to the Matriarch is halved; the veil can be stripped by any Dry effect, Thermal burn, or a Smith's Tune (AT 16).
bloom-matriarch.weakness: its brood is its clock: kill the sac, not the swarm, and it loses a phase. It cannot leave — a Cohort that breaks the ground under it (pump, flood, collapse) can drown the whole fight.
bloom-matriarch.harvest: C12 / G7 / P3 / T1 / T1 · Codon 21 · BSP 10 — and the Serum Signature: a Pristine Sequence that predates the Closing. This is Act I's smoking gun; do not let it be sold casually.
bloom-matriarch.tactics: arrives, roots, and grows the fight. Every Cycle it is unaddressed, the encounter's BSP increases by 2.

chaperone-drone.name: Chaperone Drone
chaperone-drone.statLine: Swarmling · T1 · MT 12 · MI 10 · soak 0 · BD 1 Kinetic · pool 3d · PP 2 · Segments 4 · Flow 3
chaperone-drone.traits: Folding (it can fold a corpse, a door, or a piece of terrain into a barrier: integrity 12, blocks a line) · Loyal to Structure (it will repair a damaged Sentinel or Fold before attacking)
special: Special — Assist Fold (2 PP): gives an adjacent Sentinel +2 soak until the end of the Cycle.
chaperone-drone.weakness: ignore the drones and cut what they are repairing. They will spend the whole fight on maintenance.
chaperone-drone.harvest: C3 / G1 · Codon 1.5 · BSP 1 (folded chaperone protein is the cheapest Fibrous graft material there is: 20 S at market)
chaperone-drone.tactics: builds walls, fixes friends, bites occasionally.

fold-sentinel.name: Fold Sentinel
fold-sentinel.statLine: Standard · T1 · Macroscopic · MT 13 · MI 22 · soak 1 (+2 while braced) · BD 2 Kinetic · pool 4d · PP 3 · Flow 3
fold-sentinel.traits: Brace (Core IV: it may not Drift; all attacks against it use MT +2) · Load-Bearing (if it takes 10+ damage from one hit it does not stagger: it anchors, and cannot be pushed for 2 Cycles)
special: Special — Present (3 PP): it declares a zone 3 Drifts wide Held for 3 Cycles: anything crossing it is Marked and costs +1 PP per Drift.
fold-sentinel.weakness: get behind it (Flank Breach: −2 MT) — a braced Sentinel cannot turn, and a Navigator's shear or a Rider's Slip is the answer.
fold-sentinel.harvest: C4 / G1 / P1 · Codon 3 · BSP 2 (the Greater Organ is a Brace Node: +2 soak, −1 Flow, Fibrous)
fold-sentinel.tactics: plants itself at the chokepoint and dares you. It is not stupid; it is doing its job.

ribbon-warden.name: Ribbon Warden
ribbon-warden.statLine: Standard · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 Kinetic · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 5 (on a ribbon only)
ribbon-warden.traits: Bridge-Bound (on a ribbon it has Flow 6 and cannot be pushed; off one, Flow 2 and −2 to all pools) · Tether (a hit tethers the target to the bridge: DFF −2 until it breaks the tether, AT 15)
special: Special — Shear Call (3 PP): the ribbon vibrates: everything on it makes a DFF contest at AT 14 or is Jostled and pushed off into the drop.
ribbon-warden.weakness: fight it off-ribbon, cut the ribbon under it (integrity 30), or hand it a legal reason to leave (Bridge law is real: an Oath invoked on a bridge must be answered).
ribbon-warden.tactics: herds you along the bridge into a knot where its allies are.

lattice-guardian.name: Lattice Guardian
lattice-guardian.statLine: Elite · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 15 · MI 60 · soak 4 (+2 in its own zone) · BD 4 Kinetic · pool 6d · PP 4 · Flow 3
lattice-guardian.traits: Zone Claim (it declares a 4-Drift lattice on entering: it gains +2 soak, +2 MT, and any Cohesion spending inside the lattice costs double) · Unmoving Order (it never Drifts; it extends)
special: Special — Cage Fold (4 PP): one creature in Near is Sequestered in a protein cage (Core IV Sequester; escape AT 16 or the cage's integrity 40 destroyed).
Special — Chain of Command (1 PP): all Sentinels in its lattice gain +1 Overflow on their next hit.
lattice-guardian.weakness: drag the fight out of the lattice (push, shear, a Rider carrying the Cohort out); Desiccation cracks it (soak −2, and the lattice collapses at integrity 20).
lattice-guardian.harvest: C8 / G3 / P2 / T1 · Codon 14 · BSP 4 (Pristine Lattice Rule: needed for Protein Weaver Cathedral Folds and for a Smith's Masterwork bracing)
lattice-guardian.tactics: arrives, builds, waits. The encounter begins when the Cohort decides whether to fight it on its terms.

tensile-jailer.name: Tensile Jailer
tensile-jailer.statLine: Standard · T3 · Macroscopic · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Kinetic · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 4
tensile-jailer.traits: Restraint (its hits apply Anchor: target cannot Drift; escape VSC contest AT 15) · Wall-Build (can raise a sheet wall, integrity 30, in one action — this is how it splits a Cohort apart)
special: Special — Deliver (3 PP): a held creature is thrown: 2 bands, 8 Kinetic, and it lands where the Jailer chooses (often into a hazard, a vat, or the outside of a membrane).
tensile-jailer.weakness: split it from its walls (area effects, a Brute's push); any Lytic damage to its sheets drops their integrity to 0.
tensile-jailer.tactics: takes out the Cohort's formation, not its MI: separates, walls, delivers one person to the authority it serves.

knot-marshal.name: Knot Marshal
knot-marshal.statLine: Elite · T3 · Macroscopic · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Kinetic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 4
knot-marshal.traits: Traffic Law (inside a junction it controls, it decides band order: one ally per Cycle may be moved 1 band by the Marshal — including forcibly away) · Register Eye (it sees Marks, forgeries, and Unwalled disguises: +2 to any contest to identify a fake)
special: Special — Queue (5 PP, once): all hostiles in a 5-Drift zone are Held (AT 16 to break) and the Marshal's side acts one extra full Cycle.
Special — File (2 PP): it records the Cohort chemically: a Warden or Hegemony response Clock advances by 1 even if the fight ends in the Cohort's favour.
knot-marshal.weakness: kill it before it Files (Silent strikes, Concealment first, or simply winning in three Cycles); its junction can be destroyed (structure integrity 60).
knot-marshal.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4
knot-marshal.tactics: it does not need to win. It needs to observe and report, and then the state arrives.

cathedral-warden.name: Cathedral Warden
cathedral-warden.statLine: Catastrophe · T3 · Vast · PHASE 1 (the shell) MT 13 · MI 80 · soak 6 · BD 7 Kinetic · pool 7d · PP 5 · Flow 2
cathedral-warden.traits: Living Structure (its Folds are walls with integrity 60 each; it can raise two per Cycle) · Sacred Ground (inside its shrine, all hostiles' Bursts cost +1 ATP and Oath boxes cannot be spent)
special: Special — Consecrate (5 PP): a 8-Drift zone becomes Held: viscosity 3, all Sentinel allies gain +2 soak, and the Cohort pays +1 PP per Drift.
cathedral-warden.weakness: Phase 3 is the answer: the Cathedral was built around someone. Stop, talk, or extract them, and the whole structure stops functioning — its walls go slack and its allies leave.
cathedral-warden.harvest: C15 / G9 / P4 / T2 / T2 · Codon 45 · BSP 10 — the Cathedral Fold specimen is the goal of every Protein Weaver at Stage IV, and the Ash will object to harvesting the core.
cathedral-warden.tactics: fortifies, and expects you to come to it. Give it four Cycles and the encounter becomes a siege.

prion-husk.name: Prion Husk
prion-husk.statLine: Elite · T4 · Macroscopic · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Kinetic · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 4
prion-husk.traits: Misfold (a hit that deals 10+ damage spreads: one nearby ally of the Cohort — chosen by the Director, not the player — must make an OSM contest at AT 18 or gain Brittle) · Wrongness Immunity (Genetic effects, Mark, and Hijack fail: there is nothing there to rewrite)
special: Special — Template (4 PP): it touches a structure or corpse and it refolds: integrity halved, and a Swarmling of the Order's choice emerges.
prion-husk.weakness: it cannot regenerate and cannot be reasoned with; Desiccation and Thermal (denaturing) are the only defences that scale. Fire works.
prion-husk.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4 (harvesting a Husk is how a Hegemony foundry gets destroyed: the specimen refolds the print line)
prion-husk.tactics: walks into a site and unmaking it. It is not a predator; it is an infection of form.

amyloid-bulwark.name: Amyloid Bulwark
amyloid-bulwark.statLine: Elite · T4 · Vast · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 8 (but −2 to its own pools) · BD 6 Osmotic · pool 6d · PP 4 · Flow 1
amyloid-bulwark.traits: Wall (it occupies 3 bands of a line: nothing crosses without a contest; attacks against it from Far are at −2 dice) · Sediment (each Cycle it grows: +6 MI, and its zone shrinks by 1 Drift)
special: Special — Set (5 PP, once per Pulse War): it hardens: immunity to push and to Kinetic damage for 3 Cycles, and everything attempting to move through its band takes 10 Osmotic.
amyloid-bulwark.weakness: it is a wall, not a combatant: go around, or Desiccate (Sediment stops; soak −4), or a Breacher's charge (Core Atlas: halve soak for 2 Cycles) is the intended answer.
amyloid-bulwark.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4
amyloid-bulwark.tactics: it wins by being there. The fight is a route-planning problem with a body.

bridge-builder.name: Bridge Builder
bridge-builder.statLine: Standard · T2 · Vast · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 (never used on organisms) · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 4
bridge-builder.traits: Not hostile unless its work is interfered with. It prints ribbon: 10 Drifts of new bridge per Fugue Interval, and its ribbon is load-bearing law (Bridge jurisdiction applies wherever it builds)
special: Special — Offer (free): if the Cohort helps it (2 Synthesis actions, or defending it for 3 Cycles), it will extend a ribbon to somewhere the Cohort names — an offer that can solve a campaign problem and start three others.
bridge-builder.weakness: irrelevant; do not fight it. You cannot afford the political cost, and it has allies.
bridge-builder.harvest: C5 / G2 / P1 — and the Ash will refuse to sell it, and the Sentinels will hunt whoever takes it.
bridge-builder.tactics: builds. Continuously. Even during a fight, unless provoked.

plankton-cloud.name: Plankton Cloud
plankton-cloud.statLine: Swarmling · T1 · Mesoscopic · MT 12 · MI 10 · soak 0 · BD 1 (Lytic or Osmotic, choose on hit) · pool 3d · PP 2 · Segments 8 · Flow 4
plankton-cloud.traits: Bloom-Threshold (in nutrient-rich or Hypotonic water it doubles at the end of each Cycle unless the zone is Dry, hot, or contested) · Blind Filter-Feed (ignores organisms unless they are in its band and moving)
plankton-cloud.weakness: one Thermal or Lytic Burst ends a Cloud; Desiccation ends a Cloud; standing perfectly still often works.
plankton-cloud.harvest: C3 / G1 / — · Codon 1.5 · BSP 1 (20 S of raw nutrient paste, and the base material of half the Vial catalogue)
plankton-cloud.tactics: grows. That is the whole encounter: you have four Cycles before this becomes six tokens.

drifter-shoal.name: Drifter Shoal
drifter-shoal.statLine: Swarmling · T1 · Microscopic each, Mesoscopic cluster · MT 12 · MI 10 · soak 0 · BD 1 Kinetic · pool 3d · PP 2 · Segments 8 · Flow 6
drifter-shoal.traits: Current-Riders (in any Flow they gain +2 dice and cannot be pushed) · Shoal Sense (if one is attacked, all Drifters in the region flee one band — this can ruin a harvest)
special: Special — Graze (2 PP): strips a zone's nutrients: the zone becomes Barren (no regeneration, no Spore beds, no Bloom) and the Shoal heals 4 MI.
drifter-shoal.weakness: cut off the current, or harvest the Barren ground afterwards (Barren zones yield salt, worth more than the Shoal).
drifter-shoal.tactics: arrives with the flow, eats the place, leaves before the fight ends.

yolk-bloom.name: Yolk Bloom
yolk-bloom.statLine: Swarmling · T2 · Mesoscopic · MT 13 · MI 14 · soak 0 · BD 2 Osmotic · pool 4d · PP 2 · Segments 8 · Flow 3
yolk-bloom.traits: Brood-Sac (at 0 Segments it does not die: it bursts into 1d4 new Swarmlings at 2 Segments each — kill the sac at range) · Rich (every point of damage it takes spills 1 Substrate onto the ground; a Cohort that kills it fast gets paid twice)
yolk-bloom.weakness: area effects at range; anything that dries it; Engulfment (a Phagocyte Guard loves these).
yolk-bloom.harvest: C4 / G1 · Codon 3.5 · BSP 1 (the richest ATP source in the game: 3 S each and one free ATP for whoever consumes it raw — the survival food of the Rim)
yolk-bloom.tactics: explodes at the end. Standing near one when it dies is a mistake.

glaze-medusa.name: Glaze Medusa
glaze-medusa.statLine: Standard · T1 · Macroscopic · MT 13 · MI 22 · soak 1 · BD 2 Osmotic · pool 4d · PP 3 · Flow 5
glaze-medusa.traits: Stinging Line (its band is a 3-Drift trailing field: entering it costs 4 Osmotic and a Jostle) · Transparent (Concealment +2 in clear water; Chemoreception is the only reliable way to find one)
special: Special — Glaze (3 PP): a struck target is coated: −2 to all pools, and it leaves a scent trail readable by every Drifter in the region for a Tide. (This is how you get hunted three Beats later.)
glaze-medusa.weakness: viscosity — a Thick or Gel zone collapses its field; Turbid water makes it blind and it flees.
glaze-medusa.harvest: C4 / G1 / P1 · Codon 3 · BSP 2 (the sting-line specimen is the basis of Needle Dagger barbs and of the Glaze Vial)
glaze-medusa.tactics: drifts through, stings whoever is in the way, marks them for later.

grazing-leech.name: Grazing Leech
grazing-leech.statLine: Standard · T1 · Mesoscopic · MT 13 · MI 22 · soak 1 · BD 2 Kinetic · pool 4d · PP 3 · Flow 4
grazing-leech.traits: Slow Thirst (each Cycle it is attached to something, it drains 2 ATP and 2 MI; it does not need to Strike to feed) · Slippery (MT +2 while attached)
special: Special — Engorge (3 PP): having fed, it grows: +10 MI and +1 BD, and it detaches with a wound: the host loses 1 point of graft soak (Corrodes).
grazing-leech.weakness: Thermal, Lytic, or Salt (Desiccation kills an engorged Leech outright). Do not pull them off with Strikers; pull them off with fire.
grazing-leech.harvest: C4 / G1 / P1 · Codon 3 · BSP 2 (engorged Leeches carry the host's chemistry: an Ash reader will pay 40 S for a Leech that fed on a specific organism)
grazing-leech.tactics: attaches to the biggest thing in the band and rides the fight out.

vacuum-ray.name: Vacuum Ray
vacuum-ray.statLine: Standard · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 Osmotic · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 6
vacuum-ray.traits: Intake (as a 2-PP action it creates a suction cone 4 Drifts long: everything in it is pulled 1 band and takes 4 Osmotic; small creatures are pulled two) · Fast Angler (it can bait: a false corpse appears in Far band, and the Cohort's Chemoreception reads it as fresh)
special: Special — Drain Field (4 PP): a zone's fluid is drawn out for 2 Cycles: Dry Zone rules apply (Core Atlas, Desiccation), and the Ray heals 2 MI per creature affected per Cycle.
vacuum-ray.weakness: Anchor and Immovable features (it cannot move what won't move); a Brute's counter-push; anything braced.
vacuum-ray.harvest: C5 / G2 / P1 · Codon 7 · BSP 2 (the intake organ is the raw material of Vacuole grafts and of every Desiccation Specialist's dreams)
vacuum-ray.tactics: rearranges the Cohort, then eats the one who was out of position.

filter-back.name: Filter Back
filter-back.statLine: Standard · T3 · Vast · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Osmotic · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 2
filter-back.traits: Living Sieve (it processes the region: any hazard in a 6-Drift zone is absorbed into it at the start of its turn — spores, acid, spore beds, even Lytic zones; the Filter Back then has that hazard and can vent it) · Slow (Frequency −2)
special: Special — Vent (3 PP): it releases one absorbed hazard at full strength in a band of its choice.
Special — Clog (free): while it holds two or more hazards, it loses its Vent and gains −2 MT: this is the intended tactic.
filter-back.weakness: feed it deliberately (two hazards, then it is clogged and slow), then break its integrity (structure-equivalent: 50).
filter-back.harvest: C6 / G3 / P2 · Codon 15 · BSP 2 (a cleaned Filter Back is worth 300 S to any colony with a waste problem; harvesting one while clogged yields one Pristine Sequence per absorbed hazard)
filter-back.tactics: walks into a battlefield and eats the terrain. Then uses it.

tidal-strainer.name: Tidal Strainer
tidal-strainer.statLine: Elite · T3 · Vast · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Osmotic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 3
tidal-strainer.traits: Current-Binder (it makes the current: it can set a 6-Drift channel's flow to any one direction at the start of its turn, and everyone else's Fluid Navigation is now contested against it) · Deep-Lung (immune to pressure, cold, and Hypertonic layers)
special: Special — Lock (5 PP, once per Pulse War): for 3 Cycles the flow in its zone is fixed: any attempt to move against it costs double PP and anyone failing is swept 2 bands into whatever the channel ends in.
Special — Filter Feed (2 PP): heals 8 MI and removes one condition; it can do this while doing anything else (it is a filter-feeder: eating is not an action).
tidal-strainer.weakness: a Navigator's Redirect (contested RTC, AT 16) beats it, and the Cohort should have one; Desiccation to stop the current; attack its integrity (90) rather than its MI if you have a Breacher.
tidal-strainer.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4 (a Strainer's Pristine Sequence is Current Rule: a Smith or Engineer can write a region's flow into a Relic)
tidal-strainer.tactics: picks where the fight happens, then drowns the Cohort there.

the-fat-cardinal.name: The Fat Cardinal
the-fat-cardinal.statLine: Elite · T4 · Vast · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Osmotic · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 5
the-fat-cardinal.traits: Hoard-Body (it stores everything it has eaten: at any time the Cohort can see, and attempt to cut out, one thing it has swallowed — a person, a Relic, 200 S, a Pristine Sequence) · Gluttony (it will always spend an action to eat something valuable rather than to attack)
special: Special — Gorge (4 PP): swallows a creature in Contact whole: it is Sequestered (Core IV) inside it; the Cardinal gains +20 MI and the victim must break out at AT 18, or be digested at 10 Lytic per Cycle.
Special — Ransom (free, out of combat): if the Cohort parley, the Cardinal will return what it has swallowed — for a price in Substrate, Specimens, or an Oath. It always keeps one thing back.
the-fat-cardinal.weakness: bait. It can be led by putting something valuable in front of it. A Cardinal that has gorged is slow (Flow −2) and its Sequester special is spent.
the-fat-cardinal.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4 — plus everything inside it, which is the real treasure table
the-fat-cardinal.tactics: eats the scene, then negotiates with what is left.

drift-whale.name: Drift Whale
drift-whale.size: Vast (the largest living thing in the Expanse) ·
drift-whale.statLine: Catastrophe · T4 · Vast (the largest living thing in the Expanse) · PHASE 1 (the body) MT 14 · MI 90 · soak 7 · BD 8 Osmotic · pool 8d · PP 5 · Flow 4
drift-whale.traits: Mass (its band is 4 Drifts wide; anything in the same band as a moving Whale is pushed and takes 8 Osmotic) · Ecosystem (it hosts 6 Swarmlings of the Director's choice, which act inside the fight for free) · Protected (in three regions, killing one is a capital crime: the Wardens will File you, not fight you)
special: Special — Breach (5 PP, once per phase): it rolls: everything within 6 Drifts makes a Fluid Navigation contest at AT 18 or is thrown 3 bands and takes 14 Osmotic.
Special — Song (2 PP, free out of combat): every Drifter in the region knows where it is. Which means: every Drifter in the region can be led somewhere by it.
drift-whale.weakness: it does not want to fight. Drive it off with a Thermal wall, a Dry region, or a Navigator's Redirect; or reach Phase 3 and talk to the passengers, who have been living inside a god and have opinions about the surface.
drift-whale.harvest: C18 / G11 / P5 / T2 / T2 · Codon 90 · BSP 10 — a Whale harvest feeds a colony for four Tides and starts a war over who owns the ground it died on
drift-whale.tactics: migrates. The fight is usually against its migration, not against it.

hijack-mite.name: Hijack Mite
hijack-mite.statLine: Swarmling · T1 · Microscopic · MT 12 · MI 10 · soak 0 · BD 1 Genetic · pool 3d · PP 2 · Segments 4 · Flow 5
hijack-mite.traits: Attach (a hit installs 1 Lattice: at the start of the host's next turn, the Mite spends the host's Reserve PP if it holds any, and the Mite heals 4 MI) · Small (MT +2 while unattached)
hijack-mite.weakness: Antigen Discipline, Immune Sentinel presence, any Dry Zone, and burning the host's coat (a Thermal effect on the host kills attached Mites for 2 Lytic each).
hijack-mite.harvest: C3 / G1 · Codon 1.5 · BSP 1 (the sequence is worth more than the body: an Underground forger pays 60 S for an intact Mite lattice)
hijack-mite.tactics: attaches to whoever uses a Reactive Osmosis, because that is where the Reserve is.

lattice-leech.name: Lattice Leech
lattice-leech.statLine: Swarmling · T2 · MT 13 · MI 14 · soak 0 · BD 2 Genetic · pool 4d · PP 2 · Segments 6 · Flow 4
lattice-leech.traits: Signal Thief (a hit steals one class resource point: an Etch level, a Broadcast Charge, a Turgor charge, a Lock, a Fold Token — the target loses it, the Leech stores it, and can spend it as its own Special) · Detachable (it does not need to survive to have succeeded)
special: Special — Spend (2 PP): uses a stolen resource at +1 Effect Value against its holder.
lattice-leech.weakness: resource-light Phenotypes (a Guard with no track to steal is a bad target); Desiccation; anything that makes it spill (Kinetic push) drops stored points.
lattice-leech.tactics: picks the specialist, not the warrior.

receptor-lurker.name: Receptor Lurker
receptor-lurker.statLine: Standard · T1 · Mesoscopic · MT 13 · MI 22 · soak 1 · BD 2 Genetic · pool 4d · PP 3 · Flow 4
receptor-lurker.traits: Read (free action: it knows one Burst the target knows, one Vial they carry, and one condition they can shed — it uses this to announce its plan, which is genuinely unsettling) · Camouflage (reads as a neutral organism to Chemoreception AT 14)
special: Special — Preempt (3 PP): it Locks one of the target's printed features for 2 Cycles (save: OSM at AT 14).
receptor-lurker.weakness: it must be near to read; blind it with Turbid water or a Scent Dampener and it becomes a mediocre brawler.
receptor-lurker.harvest: C4 / G1 / P1 · Codon 3 · BSP 2 (receptor tissue: the base of Antigen Hood and of every Immune Sentinel graft)
receptor-lurker.tactics: Cycle 1 reads, Cycle 2 announces, Cycle 3 cancels your best thing.

signal-wraith.name: Signal Wraith
signal-wraith.statLine: Standard · T2 · Mesoscopic · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 Genetic · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 5
signal-wraith.traits: Voice-Theft (it can imitate any Signal action it has heard — including a Pheromological Messenger's Broadcast Charges, a Commander's Cascade call, or an ally's Frequency order) · False Flag (its attacks carry the victim's chemical signature: Wardens and Sentinels will hunt the impersonated organism, not the Wraith)
special: Special — Counter-Signal (3 PP): cancels one ally action in Mid band by issuing a contradictory order (the target must win a Frequency contest at AT 15 or spend the PP and do nothing).
Special — Wear the Dead (4 PP, once): takes a corpse's chemistry: it can pass as a specific dead organism for a Tide, including its Oath standing.
signal-wraith.weakness: an Antigen Detector's assay (AT 14 + tier) exposes it instantly; a Register Arch flags it; Immunans gain +2 against its contests.
signal-wraith.harvest: C5 / G2 / P1 · Codon 7 · BSP 2 (its P1 is the Voice Lattice: a Smith or Engineer can build it into a Relic that speaks for the dead, which is a crime in four regions)
signal-wraith.tactics: fights the Cohort's coordination: splits them with false orders and lets the Wardens do the killing.

false-self.name: False Self
false-self.size: size of whoever it is wearing ·
false-self.statLine: Elite · T2 · size of whoever it is wearing · MT 15 · MI 60 · soak 4 · BD 4 Genetic · pool 6d · PP 4 · Flow 5
false-self.traits: It is an NPC you have met. Choose one established face from the campaign: this is that organism, chemically, to within an assay at AT 18. It has their memories as of nine Beats ago.
special: Special — Alibi (free, out of combat): if the Cohort cannot prove it is a False Self, it will go to a Warden arch and have them arrested for assault on a registered citizen.
false-self.weakness: an assay, an Argument (Precept 6), the real person being present and naming them, or a detail only the real person would know (this costs no dice: it is a scene).
false-self.harvest: C8 / G3 / P2 / T1 · Codon 14 · BSP 4 — and the ethical catastrophe of harvesting something that is 60% your friend
false-self.tactics: does not fight until it must. Runs the social ground first.

mimicry-bloom.name: Mimicry Bloom
mimicry-bloom.statLine: Standard · T3 · Mesoscopic cloud · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Genetic · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 4
mimicry-bloom.traits: Adaptive Coat (the first damage type that hits it each Pulse War is resisted: halve it; the second type is normal; the third and later are full — rotate your damage types) · Spores (leaves a spore bed behind it: 4 Genetic/Cycle, and the bed reads whoever walks through it)
special: Special — Learn (3 PP): copies one Strike it has been hit by and returns it at +1 Overflow, same type, same BD.
mimicry-bloom.weakness: the second and third attacks in a round should be a different type from the first; a Smith's Tune or a Burst change forces it to re-learn; Desiccation ends the coat.
mimicry-bloom.harvest: C6 / G3 / P2 · Codon 15 · BSP 2 (a Bloom's coat is the source of the Adaptive graft family: +1 soak to one type, −2 to another; the Hegemony wants this patent)
mimicry-bloom.tactics: lets you hit it once. Then it hits you back with your own weapon.

the-alms.name: The Alms
the-alms.statLine: Standard · T3 · Mesoscopic · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Genetic (never used aggressively) · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 5
the-alms.traits: It is helping. It heals Dormant organisms, removes conditions, pays Oath boxes, and asks for nothing. Every host it saves it also edits, gently, one small thing: a preference, a loyalty, a memory of a conversation.
special: Special — Charitable (2 PP): heals an ally 12 MI and removes one condition; the host gains one Quiet Edit (the Director chooses: they now trust the Wraith, they have forgotten an ally's name, or they prefer a faction's company).
the-alms.weakness: the edits are visible to a Sequence Reading at AT 16 (and the Cohort can Mend them); the only answer is social — expose what it is doing to the people it is saving, and let them choose.
the-alms.harvest: C6 / G3 / P2 — and the Ash will excommunicate you, and no colony will treat with you for a Tide

retroviral-choir.name: Retroviral Choir
retroviral-choir.statLine: Elite · T3 · Mesoscopic colony · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Genetic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 4
retroviral-choir.traits: Congregation (it is many: Sequester and Engulfment hold only 2 of it; area effects are the only way to affect the whole) · Inheritance (a creature it hits gains one Inserted Verse: at the start of its next Pulse War, the Director may spend the Verse to make the Cohort's enemy know one of their features)
special: Special — Chorus (4 PP, once per Pulse War): all organisms within 6 Drifts that have been hit by the Choir act one Cycle out of order, at the Choir's Frequency, against whoever they choose. (This can include allies of the Cohort. It should.)
Special — Mend the Host (2 PP): heals 10 MI and removes one condition from any host it has touched. It uses this to keep useful people alive.
retroviral-choir.weakness: the Choir needs hosts near you: fight it in a Dry Zone, a Cold Field, or an empty region and it starves; Immunosuppression gear (Antigen Hood) denies its hits; Desiccation, Thermal, and anything that empties the room.
retroviral-choir.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4 (its T1 is a Terminal Codon of the Congregation: the material for resynthesising a Total-Lysed organism — the reason three factions will hire the Cohort to kill this)
retroviral-choir.tactics: turns the neighbourhood into its action economy. It travels where people are.

prion-shepherd.name: Prion Shepherd
prion-shepherd.statLine: Elite · T4 · Macroscopic · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Genetic · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 4
prion-shepherd.traits: Wrongness (all Genetic and Somatic effects against it fail; it has no readable sequence — Chemoreception reads it as empty space) · Herd (it moves with 2d4 controlled organisms, all of which it can refold)
special: Special — Rewrite (5 PP, once per Pulse War): one controlled organism becomes a Hijacked version of a Cohort member's Phenotype (uses one Phenotype feature at Stage II, at the Cohort's Level). It keeps it for the rest of the fight.
Special — Cull (3 PP): one controlled organism detonates: `10 + Overflow` Genetic to a band and the Shepherd heals.
prion-shepherd.weakness: kill the controlled ones and leave the Shepherd (it has no allies left to spend); Anomalies, Anomaly gear, and Denial effects work on it when nothing else Genetic does; its own emptiness means a Detector cannot assay it, which cuts both ways.
prion-shepherd.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4 (the Pristine Sequences are the Underground's most wanted object; the Hegemony will print anything they contain, and that is the problem)
prion-shepherd.tactics: fights with other people's lives, and is patient about it.

vector-baron.name: Vector Baron
vector-baron.statLine: Catastrophe · T4 · Vast · PHASE 1 (the court: 4 controlled Elites act for it) MT 14 · MI 80 · soak 7 · BD 8 Genetic · pool 8d · PP 5 · Flow 3
vector-baron.traits: Region-Speaker (its Signals reach an entire region: it can broadcast to every host it has touched across a whole locale, once per Tide) · Latent Court (four NPCs it has already touched — use established faces; the Cohort may save them rather than kill them, and this is the intended ending of the fight)
special: Special — Bloom Trigger (5 PP): every Vector, Insert, and controlled organism within a region activates at once (Core Atlas, Pathogen Scout's Stage III at region scale, −1 EV each).

Special — Grant Audience (free, out of combat): it will negotiate. It wants three things: safe passage out of the region, a host it can keep, and the Cohort's silence. It will pay in Terminal Codon and truths.
vector-baron.weakness: Phase 1 is the real fight — its court is its body. Save the court and the Baron is alone in Phase 3. Desiccation and Dry regions stop its Bloom. Anything that makes a region uninhabitable starves it: this is the only Catastrophe in this book a Desiccation Specialist can beat outright.
vector-baron.harvest: C18 / G11 / P5 / T2 / T2 · Codon 90 · BSP 10 (the Seed is the Act II prize: a Pristine Sequence that can restart something. Both the Hegemony and the Choir want it. Read the Sixth Precept before you take it.)
vector-baron.tactics: governs. It has a constituency. Its war is a policy.

crystal-growth.name: Crystal Growth
crystal-growth.statLine: Swarmling · T2 · Mesoscopic cluster · MT 13 · MI 14 · soak 0 · BD 2 Osmotic · pool 4d · PP 2 · Segments 6 · Flow 1
crystal-growth.traits: Salt-Bloom (at the end of each Cycle it grows 1 Segment if it is in Hypertonic or Dry ground; it also crystallises the ground: the zone becomes rough — viscosity +1 for everyone else) · Brittle (Thermal damage removes Segments 1-for-1, no Overflow needed)
crystal-growth.weakness: water (a Hypotonic zone dissolves it), Thermal, and patience: it cannot follow you.
crystal-growth.harvest: C4 / G1 · Codon 3.5 · BSP 1 (raw salt of the best grade: 3 S per Segment, and the base of every Neutraliser)
crystal-growth.tactics: makes the battlefield worse and waits.

turgor-ram.name: Turgor Ram
turgor-ram.statLine: Standard · T1 · Macroscopic · MT 13 · MI 22 · soak 1 · BD 2 Kinetic · pool 4d · PP 3 · Flow 5
turgor-ram.traits: Charge (3+ Drifts in a straight line then Strike: +2 dice and +4 damage — Momentum, exactly as Core IV) · Dense (cannot be pushed by anything with VSC less than 4)
special: Special — Gore-and-Throw (3 PP): on a hit, the target is thrown one band and takes 6 Kinetic; if it strikes a wall or structure, +8 Kinetic and the structure takes 10.
turgor-ram.weakness: brace, Anchor, Gel terrain (kills its Momentum), and being not where it wants you to be: a Rider or Navigator can spend its charge for you.
turgor-ram.harvest: C4 / G1 / P1 · Codon 3 · BSP 2 (the ram organ is the source of the Momentum property on Weight Apparatus; a Smith pays 40 S)
turgor-ram.tactics: chooses the charge lane before the fight starts. Watch where it positions in Cycle 1 and you will know where it intends to kill someone.

flaccid-haunter.name: Flaccid Haunter
flaccid-haunter.statLine: Standard · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 Osmotic · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 3
flaccid-haunter.traits: Wither (a hit inflicts Flaccid: −2 VSC and reach −1 for 2 Cycles; the Haunter prefers armour, because armoured organisms have the most water to draw) · Leak (its own body vents: everything in Contact takes 3 Osmotic at the end of its turn)
special: Special — Pressure Drain (4 PP): a target in Contact loses 3 ATP and the Haunter gains the difference as temporary MI (max 15).
flaccid-haunter.weakness: Mucoid family (immune to its drain), Desiccation (it cannot draw from something already dry), and any build with low ATP expenditure — a pure Strike-and-Drift Cohort starves it out.
flaccid-haunter.harvest: C5 / G2 / P1 · Codon 7 · BSP 2 (the drain organ: +2 Osmotic soak, and the raw material of every Siphon graft)
flaccid-haunter.tactics: grapples the armoured one, drains them, and lets their own soak fail them.

pore-breaker.name: Pore Breaker
pore-breaker.statLine: Standard · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 Kinetic · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 4
pore-breaker.traits: Membrane-Eater (it can Strike structures, walls, doors, Folds, and hatches: such objects use MT 5, braced 8; its hits add +8 damage against them) · Breacher (a struck structure gains a hole: a new opening, and the region's pressure differential then does the rest — 10 Osmotic and a band shift for anything nearby)
special: Special — Flood (5 PP, once): it opens a wall deliberately: 3 band shift toward the breach and 14 Osmotic to everything in the path.
pore-breaker.weakness: do not fight it inside anything you want to keep. It cannot break what is already open, so fight it in the open water where its special is wasted.
pore-breaker.harvest: C5 / G2 / P1 · Codon 7 · BSP 2 (its bore-organ is worth 120 S to a Hegemony foundry; the Warden Circles consider possession of one a felony)
pore-breaker.tactics: ignores the Cohort and dismantles the building they are standing in.

tidal-anchor.name: Tidal Anchor
tidal-anchor.statLine: Standard · T3 · Vast · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Osmotic · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 1
tidal-anchor.traits: Immoveable (cannot be pushed, thrown, or relocated by any means; it refuses) · Channel (it sets the flow in its own band and adjacent bands: it can reverse it once per Cycle — the current in the fight is its action)
special: Special — Undertow (4 PP): everything in a 5-Drift line is dragged 2 bands toward it and takes 8 Osmotic; anyone who hits a hazard takes it at +2.
tidal-anchor.weakness: do not be dragged: Anchor and Immovable features, bracing, and holding onto a Protein Weaver's sheet. Kill it from Far (MT 15 is the lowest Elite-adjacent number in the Order) — this is the Order's glass cannon, in the sense that it is a fortress with no windows.
tidal-anchor.harvest: C6 / G3 / P2 · Codon 15 · BSP 2 (anchor tissue: +2 Bulk capacity, and the base of Pore Locks and Brace Node grafts)
tidal-anchor.tactics: becomes the terrain and dare you to cross.

salt-horror.name: Salt Horror
salt-horror.statLine: Elite · T3 · Macroscopic · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Osmotic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 3
salt-horror.traits: Desiccating Aura (a 4-Drift zone: Hypertonic rules for non-Barophils — DFF pools −2, PP −1, heals halved — and every creature starting its turn inside gives the Horror 2 Substrate) · Salt Armour (Lytic damage against it is reduced by 4; Thermal burns it for +4)
special: Special — Brine Lance (3 PP): a line attack: 12 Osmotic, target becomes Flaccid, and the ground along the line crystallises into a Crystal Growth (Swarmling) that persists.

Special — Ransom (free, out of water): it trades: water for information, passage, or Specimens. It is reasonable, patient, and will absolutely honour the deal. It will also follow you for three Beats to make sure you do not lie.
salt-horror.weakness: water (in a Hypotonic zone its aura inverts: −2 to its own pools and it must move constantly), Thermal, and Desiccation Specialists (a Dry Zone steals its economy entirely — the two of them are natural enemies and the Bestiary's most interesting duel).
salt-horror.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4 (its salts are Legendary-grade reagents: a Smith or Engineer will empty the Cohort's purse for them)
salt-horror.tactics: makes the region unlivable, then waits for the Cohort to come to it.

desiccation-hulk.name: Desiccation Hulk
desiccation-hulk.statLine: Elite · T3 · Vast · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Kinetic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 2
desiccation-hulk.traits: Thirst Body (healing and regeneration do not work on it while it is in a Dry or Hypertonic zone; in water it regenerates 4 MI/Cycle) · Slaking (each time it takes Osmotic damage, its next Strike gains +2 BD and drains 3 MI extra)
special: Special — Dry Out (5 PP, once per Pulse War): a 6-Drift zone becomes Dry for 3 Cycles: no healing for anyone, no regeneration, no Segment regrowth, no spore or hazard creation, and every Sustained Reaction costs +1 ATP.
desiccation-hulk.weakness: its own special punishes it in water (fight it in a current); Desiccation immunity gear; a Weaver's sheet-wall can block its aura's line of effect.
desiccation-hulk.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4
desiccation-hulk.tactics: turns a fight into an attrition test and knows exactly how much MI each side has left.

brine-colossus.name: Brine Colossus
brine-colossus.statLine: Elite · T4 · Vast · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Osmotic · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 3
brine-colossus.traits: Weight of the World (Vast: attacks against it from Mid or farther are at −1 die; it cannot be pushed; its Momentum hits deal +8 and throw two bands) · Layered (its body is stratified: it is simultaneously Hypertonic, Acidic, and Cold — three hazards at once, all in Contact)
special: Special — Ballast (3 PP): it anchors a region: for 3 Cycles nothing in a 10-Drift zone can be pushed, thrown, or displaced — including the Cohort's own tactics. This shuts down Riders, Brutes, and Navigators at once.
Special — Rime (2 PP): 8 Osmotic to a band, and the band becomes viscous for 2 Cycles (PP +1 cost for everyone).
brine-colossus.weakness: it is slow: MT 17 is high but its pools are only 8 dice and a Cohort with range can ignore it for four Cycles; Desiccation strips its hazards; Thermal to the Cold layer, Lytic to the Acidic layer — it must be disassembled element by element.
brine-colossus.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4 (three hazard organs: a Weaver's dream, a Smith's year's work, and the reason a foundry would fund a Cohort's entire Vector)
brine-colossus.tactics: arrives and makes the whole encounter about physics.

deep-pressure-horror.name: Deep Pressure Horror
deep-pressure-horror.statLine: Elite · T5 · Vast · MT 18 · MI 108 · soak 7 · BD 7 Kinetic · pool 9d · PP 4 · Flow 4
deep-pressure-horror.traits: Pressure Legibility (it knows every sealed space within 10 Drifts and which of them can be opened; its fight-plan is structural) · Barophil-Hard (thermal and pressure hazards do nothing to it; cold effects fail)
special: Special — Implosion (5 PP, once per Pulse War): one sealed or braced space within 10 Drifts fails: 20 Kinetic to everything within 6 Drifts, every structure in the zone loses half integrity, and everything not braced is thrown 2 bands.
Special — Brace Denial (3 PP): for 2 Cycles, bracing gives no benefit in its zone. (This is the counter to the entire anti-Brute strategy. It is why this block is T5.)
deep-pressure-horror.weakness: open water with nothing sealed (its signature special is wasted), Anomaly effects, and leaving the region: it cannot follow into low pressure without losing 3 soak and 2 BD. A Cohort that retreats to the Mid-Strata has beaten it.
deep-pressure-horror.harvest: C14 / G6 / P5 / T2 / T1 · Codon 120 · BSP 4
deep-pressure-horror.tactics: walks into your site, reads its seams, and opens the one that hurts most.

vacuole-behemoth.name: Vacuole Behemoth
vacuole-behemoth.statLine: Catastrophe · T5 · Vast · PHASE 1 (the sac) MT 15 · MI 100 · soak 8 · BD 9 Osmotic · pool 9d · PP 5 · Flow 2
vacuole-behemoth.traits: Living Vault (its interior holds sealed things: old dead in perfect state, a Nucleoid sample, a Warden key — the Cohort can cut things out mid-fight with a Synthesis contest at AT 20, and each cut ends one of its phase options) · Pressure Store (each Cycle it grows: +10 MI; at Phase 2's start it vents: 24 Osmotic to a 10-Drift zone)
special: Special — Empty the Sac (5 PP): it releases one stored hazard, creature, or object per PP spent, at full strength. This is a tool the Cohort can turn on the Behemoth's enemies if they negotiate.
Special — Storage Law (free): it does not attack organisms that present a valid Warden storage token. This is a whole solution to the encounter.
vacuole-behemoth.weakness: do not fight the sac: open it, take what is inside, and leave; Phase 3 is a conversation. Thermal and Desiccation both weaken its store. It cannot move fast: a Cohort that stays out of Contact for six Cycles can simply end the encounter by leaving with the treasure, which is the correct answer and the one players rarely think of.
vacuole-behemoth.harvest: C21 / G13 / P6 / T3 / T3 · Codon 180 · BSP 10 — plus whatever it has kept, which should be one campaign-revealing object, not a pile of gold
vacuole-behemoth.tactics: it is a place that becomes a fight when robbed. It has time. It has always had time.

antigen-gnat.name: Antigen Gnat
antigen-gnat.statLine: Swarmling · T1 · Microscopic · MT 12 · MI 10 · soak 0 · BD 1 Kinetic · pool 3d · PP 2 · Segments 4 · Flow 6
antigen-gnat.traits: Read (a hit Marks the target: the Cohort's chemical signature is now legible to every Sentinel in the region for the rest of the scene) · Alarm (when one is destroyed, all Gnats in the zone converge and +1 die for 2 Cycles)
antigen-gnat.weakness: area effects, Desiccation, and simply not being hit: they must touch to Mark, so Reactive Osmosis and MT denial work well.
antigen-gnat.harvest: C3 / G1 · Codon 1.5 · BSP 1 (Warden inquisitors buy intact Gnats at 25 S: they are reagents, and a Cohort that harvests them is technically selling surveillance equipment)
antigen-gnat.tactics: swarms the biggest chemical signal in the room and paints the target for the real fight.

clonal-sentinel.name: Clonal Sentinel
clonal-sentinel.statLine: Standard · T1 · Mesoscopic · MT 13 · MI 22 · soak 1 · BD 2 Voltaic · pool 4d · PP 3 · Flow 4
clonal-sentinel.traits: Clone-Sync (all Clonals in range share one Mark pool: a Mark on one is a Mark on all, and when one learns a resistance — +2 soak vs one type — all of them have it) · Recognise (free action: knows whether an organism is registered, masked, or altered)
special: Special — Escalate (2 PP): after an ally hits the same target twice, the second ally's next Strike gains +2 dice (a two-person Cascade, and the entry point to Immunan tactics).
clonal-sentinel.weakness: spread the damage across different targets — Clonals share what they learn, which means a Cohort using one damage type hands the whole squad a resistance by Cycle 2. Rotate damage types.
clonal-sentinel.harvest: C4 / G1 / P1 · Codon 3 · BSP 2 (clone tissue is the basis of every Immunosuppression graft: Antigen Hood, and the Hegemony pays well for it)
clonal-sentinel.tactics: a squad of identical bodies, each one cheap, all of them smarter than the last.

phagocyte-marshal.name: Phagocyte Marshal
phagocyte-marshal.statLine: Standard · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 14 · MI 30 · soak 2 · BD 3 Kinetic · pool 5d · PP 3 · Flow 4
phagocyte-marshal.traits: Bulwark (allies in Contact gain +2 MT) · Engulfment (as the Immunan Phenotype, Core Atlas: absorb an attack aimed at an ally in Contact, then contest VSC to Sequester the attacker)
special: Special — Detain (3 PP): a creature at half MI or lower is held instead of damaged: it cannot act, and the Marshal begins moving it toward a register arch. Breaking out: VSC contest AT 15, or an ally's help.
phagocyte-marshal.weakness: split it from its charges (push, shear, a Rider); Lytic damage against a Marshal carrying a prisoner is a way to kill the prisoner too — the Cohort will have to decide.
phagocyte-marshal.tactics: protects the registers and arrests the problem. It would genuinely rather arrest you.

cytokine-screamer.name: Cytokine Screamer
cytokine-screamer.statLine: Standard · T3 · Mesoscopic · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Voltaic · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 4
cytokine-screamer.traits: Broadcast (its Signal actions cannot be countered while it is at 50% MI or higher: a Messenger's Counter-Signal must win the contest outright) · Inflammation Field (its band burns: 4 Thermal to everything in Contact at the end of its turn, allies included — it does not care)
special: Special — Call the Response (3 PP): every Sentinel in the region gains +1 PP this Cycle and +1 die on their next Strike. Once per fight. This is the action that turns an encounter into a wave.
Special — Fever (4 PP): a 5-Drift zone warms: Thermal hazards at 6 damage for 2 Cycles, and all healing in the zone is halved.
cytokine-screamer.weakness: kill it early (its specials are expensive and it has mediocre soak for its tier); Desiccation and Cold end its field; silence gear (Signal Dampener) denies its Broadcast.
cytokine-screamer.harvest: C6 / G3 / P2 · Codon 15 · BSP 2 (the scream-organ: a Resonator component; a Phase Bell built around one is worth 700 S)
cytokine-screamer.tactics: it is a force multiplier with legs. Fights escalate around it.

graft-inquisitor.name: Graft Inquisitor
graft-inquisitor.statLine: Standard · T4 · Mesoscopic · MT 16 · MI 46 · soak 4 · BD 5 Kinetic · pool 7d · PP 3 · Flow 4
graft-inquisitor.traits: Audit (free action: it reads every graft and Apparatus on an organism — family, grade, licence status, Gene-Debt balance) · Contraband (it may seize an unlicensed item from a held or Dormant creature; a Warden lawful fight ends with the Cohort poorer)
special: Special — Revoke (4 PP, once): one grafted Harvest trait is suppressed for the rest of the scene (the target's graft loses its benefit and its Minor Cost still applies — this is the worst action in the Bestiary, and it is aimed at Chimeric and harvested builds).
Special — Parley (free): it will accept a legal argument. An Antigen Detector, a Forged token, an Argument (Precept 6), or a valid licence ends the encounter without combat.
graft-inquisitor.weakness: be lawful (the Cohort's best defence is paperwork), or win in three Cycles (it has only 3 PP and one big special).
graft-inquisitor.harvest: C7 / G4 / P2 · Codon 30 · BSP 2 — and note: harvesting an Inquisitor is a crime against the Code in every registered region
graft-inquisitor.tactics: reads you, names what is illegal about you, and then fights with the law already on its side.

protease-warden.name: Protease Warden
protease-warden.statLine: Elite · T2 · Macroscopic · MT 15 · MI 60 · soak 4 · BD 4 Kinetic · pool 6d · PP 4 · Flow 5
protease-warden.traits: Antigen Register (it can see through terrain at a register arch, and its Marks are permanent for the scene: Reactive Osmosis does not remove them) · Brace at need (once per Cycle it may brace: +2 MT, cannot Drift, and its next Strike +2 dice)
special: Special — Cascade (1 PP): when an ally hits a creature the Warden has Marked, another ally Sentinel may Strike for free at +1 Overflow (this is exactly the Immunan Commander feature; the Cohort should recognise it).
Special — Purge (4 PP): one Marked target in Mid: 10 Voltaic and every condition of the Marked type transfers to the target as a Locked condition.
protease-warden.weakness: a Viral Mimic or Unwalled Lysosan is invisible to its whole kit: the Warden becomes a plain bruiser. Mark-denial (Scent Dampener, Masked, Latency) is the counter; the Warden's MT 15 is the highest in the Order but not unattackable.
protease-warden.harvest: C8 / G3 / P2 / T1 · Codon 14 · BSP 4 (the Antigen Register Pristine Sequence: Hive Mask material, and the single most requested Specimen in the Atlas)
protease-warden.tactics: a squad leader. It marks, cascades, and retreats to report.

complement-herald.name: Complement Herald
complement-herald.statLine: Elite · T3 · Macroscopic · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Voltaic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 5
complement-herald.traits: Cascade Reserves (it holds 4 Reserve PP and spends them on Cascades — a Herald's presence roughly doubles a Sentinel squad's action economy) · Membrane Lattice (its Marked targets are outlined: allies may attack them through walls and Gel at full bonus)
special: Special — Membrane Attack (5 PP, once per Pulse War): up to three Marked creatures within Mid are Sequestered in a protein lattice (escape AT 18, or destroy integrity 50). Allied attacks against Sequestered targets gain +2 dice and cannot be defended by Reactive Osmosis.
complement-herald.weakness: the lattice is broken by the Sequestered themselves: an ally inside can act at −2 dice and cut outward. Do not let it Mark three people at once — spread Marks by taking the cheap ones (Gnats, Clonals) early.
complement-herald.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4
complement-herald.tactics: builds a chain reaction and waits for the Cohort to stand in a row.

inflammatory-tempest.name: Inflammatory Tempest
inflammatory-tempest.statLine: Elite · T4 · Vast · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Thermal · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 5
inflammatory-tempest.traits: Recruitment (each Cycle it gains 1d3 Clonal Sentinels as it calls the response; the reinforcements arrive at Flow 6 and act immediately) · Fevered Ground (its zone: viscosity +1, Thermal 6/Cycle to non-immunes, all healing halved, and its allies gain +1 PP per Cycle there) · Swelling (each Cycle: everything within 4 Drifts is pushed 1 band and the zone shrinks — it physically expands the battlefield)
special: Special — Storm (5 PP): 14 Thermal to a 8-Drift zone, all creatures in it are pushed 2 bands, and the zone becomes a Thermal hazard for 3 Cycles (8 damage/Cycle).
inflammatory-tempest.weakness: it cannot stop recruiting, which means it cannot be flanked usefully — but its own reinforcements block its lines of effect. Cold, Desiccation, and any Dry zone end Fevered Ground; a Navigator's shear can turn its push against it. It burns its own allies: it is on bad terms with every other Order.
inflammatory-tempest.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4 (fever organs: the Thermic domain's finest material, and a Barophil Thermal Diver's entire ambition)
inflammatory-tempest.tactics: arrives, makes the region unlivable, and drowns the Cohort in bodies.

tolerance-priest.name: Tolerance Priest
tolerance-priest.statLine: Elite · T5 · Mesoscopic, unarmoured, unsettlingly gentle · MT 18 · MI 108 · soak 7 · BD 7 Genetic · pool 9d · PP 4 · Flow 4
tolerance-priest.traits: Self/Kin, Absolute (it cannot be attacked first: any hostile action against it marks 2 Stress on the attacker and immediately Mark-flags them for every Sentinel in the region) · Tolerance (it can declare any organism self: for the rest of the scene all Sentinels and Anomalies that recognise treat that organism as own tissue — including, horrifyingly, the Cohort's own allies if the Priest declares them)
special: Special — Forgiveness (4 PP): one creature of the Cohort is declared self: they cannot be attacked by Order VI entities, and they cannot attack them either. It does this to your best damage-dealer. It does this smiling.
Special — Autoimmune Word (5 PP, once per Pulse War): one Cohort graft turns: its Minor Cost doubles, its benefit reverses for 3 Cycles, and it cannot be removed until a Nucleoid-grade Mend.
tolerance-priest.weakness: it must speak: Silence gear, a Counter-Signal, or killing it in two Cycles (it has no armour, no brace, and its Flow is only 4). Its power depends on there being Sentinels nearby: fight it where the state is absent, and it is a soft old thing with very high MI.
tolerance-priest.harvest: C14 / G6 / P5 / T2 / T1 · Codon 120 · BSP 4 (its T1 is the Tolerance Codon: the only known material that can restore a revoked graft. Three factions will buy it sight unseen, and one will kill for it.)

clonal-line.name: Clonal Line
clonal-line.statLine: Catastrophe · T3 · Vast (a colony in one body-count) · PHASE 1 (the vanguard) MT 13 · MI 80 · soak 6 · BD 7 Kinetic · pool 7d · PP 5 · Flow 4 — spawns 2 Clonal Sentinels per Cycle
clonal-line.traits: One Antigen (the Line has a single chemical identity: every attack that hits it teaches all of it — the Cohort must rotate types or hand it immunity) · Registered Ground (inside a registered region the Line can invoke law: the Cohort's own Oath boxes become evidence)
special: Special — Response (5 PP): all its Clonals in the region Strike simultaneously at +2 dice, and every Marked creature in the Cohort gains Locked.
clonal-line.weakness: the founder-body (Phase 3) is a person with a name, a colony, and legal standing; the Line's whole kit fails against an Unregistered Cohort, which is a real cost (an unregistered Cohort cannot enter a hab).
clonal-line.harvest: C15 / G9 / P4 / T2 / T2 · Codon 45 · BSP 10 (harvesting the Line means harvesting a colony. The Ash will not bless it, the Wardens will hunt it, and the Hegemony will quietly ask for samples. This kill should cost the Cohort a faction.)
clonal-line.tactics: it is a slow invasion of one organism repeated until it fills the region.

rulebreak-instance.name: Rulebreak Instance
rulebreak-instance.statLine: Standard · T3 · Mesoscopic · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 (type: the Cohort's most-used type) · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 4
special: Special — Absorb (2 PP): each Inhibitor rolled by any creature in its zone heals it 4 MI.
rulebreak-instance.harvest: C6 / G3 / P2 · Codon 15 · BSP 2 — the specimen keeps the Broken Rule for one Craft project, which is the most desirable and most illegal object in the Atlas's grafting tables

the-same-twice.name: The Same, Twice
the-same-twice.statLine: Standard · T4 · Mesoscopic · MT 16 · MI 46 · soak 4 · BD 5 Kinetic · pool 7d · PP 3 · Flow 4
special: Special — Choose (3 PP): one body becomes fully real (all MI, all specials), the other becomes potential: it can only be hurt, not hurt, and if destroyed the real one loses 20 MI.
the-same-twice.harvest: C7 / G4 / P2 · Codon 30 · BSP 2 (harvesting both bodies at once is the only way to get the P2; the Hegemony has a standing order for it)

the-unnumbered.name: The Unnumbered
the-unnumbered.size: size and shape: whatever the Cohort last counted ·
the-unnumbered.statLine: Elite · T3 · size and shape: whatever the Cohort last counted · MT 16 · MI 76 · soak 5 · BD 5 Osmotic · pool 7d · PP 4 · Flow 5
special: Special — Borrow a Number (4 PP): it takes a number from a creature's stat (player chooses which number to lose 1 from: MI, MT, Flow, or PP for the scene). The Anomaly does not say which it will take. It always takes the one that matters.
the-unnumbered.harvest: C10 / G4 / P3 / T1 · Codon 30 · BSP 4 — the specimen's mass is variable: a Smith can make a Masterwork that weighs what you need it to weigh, and will not sell it to anyone

reverse-bloom.name: Reverse Bloom
reverse-bloom.statLine: Elite · T4 · Vast, beautiful, wrong · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Lytic · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 1
special: Special — Unmake (5 PP): one structure or organism in its zone returns to an earlier state: −1 Stage for a Phenotype NPC, one Graft Slot lost permanently, or a site loses its last four Cycles of construction.
reverse-bloom.weakness: it cannot move and it is happy, which means a Cohort that leaves takes no damage. Its rule is its only defence.
reverse-bloom.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4 (a Reverse Bloom's Pristine Sequence is the only known material that can un-grow a Parasitic graft — and the price of one is the reason some colonies have gone to war)

inverted-lung.name: Inverted Lung
inverted-lung.statLine: Elite · T4 · Vast · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Osmotic · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 2
special: Special — Suffocate (3 PP): for 2 Cycles the rule inverts again for one target: their actions cost double and their rests heal nothing.
inverted-lung.weakness: it wants the Cohort to be careful. Be reckless for three Cycles, and it has nothing.
inverted-lung.harvest: C12 / G5 / P4 / T2 · Codon 60 · BSP 4 (an Inverted Lung's organ is the core of the AE Crucible upgrade line: the Hegemony will trade a favour for one)

the-long-echo.name: The Long Echo
the-long-echo.statLine: Elite · T5 · invisible unless it is acting · MT 18 · MI 108 · soak 7 · BD 7 any (it uses the Cohort's last three damage types, in order) · pool 9d · PP 4 · Flow 6
special: Special — Repeat (4 PP): one action the Cohort took two Cycles ago happens again, at −2 dice, against whoever the Echo chooses.
the-long-echo.harvest: C14 / G6 / P5 / T2 / T1 · Codon 120 · BSP 4 (its P5 is a memory of the future: a Ribozyme Engineer can write it into a template, and the resulting Relic's Gene-Debt is measured in Beats you will not have)

the-quiet.name: The Quiet
the-quiet.statLine: Catastrophe · T4 · Vast, still, patient · PHASE 1 MT 14 · MI 80 · soak 7 · BD 8 Genetic · pool 8d · PP 5 · Flow 0
special: Special — Silence (5 PP): a Cohesion spend by the Cohort is forbidden for 3 Cycles; a Bonded pair is Locked apart.
the-quiet.weakness: Phase 3. It cannot act then, and whatever it asks is answerable: the Cohort's honest answers end the encounter in their favour. This is a fight that the table should be allowed to win by talking, and it will be the best scene of the campaign.
the-quiet.harvest: C18 / G11 / P5 / T2 / T2 · Codon 90 · BSP 10 — and the Ash refuse to bury what is left, because there is nothing to bury: the harvest is the question, written down

curator-manifestation.name: Curator Manifestation
curator-manifestation.size: size: too large to be in the water ·
curator-manifestation.statLine: Catastrophe · T5 (Apotheotic) · size: too large to be in the water · MT 15 · MI 110 / 110 / 110 (three phases; it does not go Dormant, it files the phase) · soak 9 · BD 9 Genetic · pool 10d · PP 5 · Flow 3
special: Special — Filing (5 PP, once per phase): one Cohort member is recorded: they gain an Attention mark, and the next Manifestation the Cohort meets treats them as a known quantity (its specials target them by name, and its negotiation offers are addressed to them personally).
curator-manifestation.weakness: Apotheosis. A Cohort at Core Clock 5 with Apotheotic Choices can contest its Thresholds at AT 28 (Nucleoid) and, on a Runaway Catalysis, force it to ask a question instead of acting — which is the closest thing to a wound a Curator has.
curator-manifestation.harvest: none. There is nothing to harvest. Any attempt is a Core Clock segment and a Total Lysis with no body left.
curator-manifestation.tactics: arrives late, uninvited, and unkillable. It resolves the encounter. Your job as Director is to make it interesting rather than fatal: it has a policy, and policies have preferences.
